articles.title: Apple’s latest sci-fi series Pluribus luxuriates in its mystery
articles.summary: Pluribus is the new show from Breaking Bad creator Vince Gilligan, and it starts streaming on Apple TV on November 7th.
articles.body: Toward the end of the first episode of Pluribus, Carol (Rhea Seehorn), a woman put in a bizarre and impossible scenario, asks a very straightforward question: “What the fuck is happening?” It’s something you’ll likely be asking yourself a lot while watching. I certainly did. But that ongoing sense of mystery, and the measured pace with which Pluribus reveals itself, is one of the best parts of the new series from Breaking Bad creator Vince Gilligan. I can’t tell you a lot about Pluribus just yet — but I can tell you that being bewildered is part of the appeal. Okay, so what can I tell you? Carol is a successful writer of fantasy novels — excuse me, “speculative historical romance literature” — and she hates both her work and her audience. She wants to do something more meaningful, but the money she rakes in from her books makes it hard to make the switch. Despite being rich and successful, and having a caring partner who doubles as her very capable manager (Miriam Shor), Carol is mostly miserable, though she’s largely able to fake it in public. --- Join me for some spoiler-heavy discussion on November 10th While I did my best to keep this early review as free of spoilers as possible, Pluribus is really a show that begs for a deeper discussion. But I’ll need your help. So check back on The Verge on Monday, November 10th, after the first two episodes premiere and you’ve had a chance to watch, when I’ll be hosting a book club-style chat for Verge subscribers, where we can all talk about Apple’s latest foray into sci-fi. --- But all that changes when… something happens. I don’t want to get too deep into spoilers before the show premieres (the first two episodes are streaming on November 7th), but the conceit of Pluribus is that following a global event that is almost apocalyptic in nature, nearly every person on Earth is inflicted with a dose of unyielding happiness. They become peaceful and collaborative and unable to cause harm to any living thing. Carol remains unaffected — but not for a lack of trying. Early on, when she’s outside of a hospital that looks like a warzone, the “others” — which is what I’ll call these happy folks for now — try to bring her over to their side. When it doesn’t work and she freaks out, they all say in unison, “We just want to help, Carol!” [Image: It’s extremely creepy and puts Carol in a difficult position. Normally she just complains about everything wrong with the world, but now she’s just about the only person who can actually save it. Of course, how she goes about that isn’t so easy to figure out. One person up against a few billion puts her at a serious disadvantage. The thing is, while the others want Carol to be a part of their group, they also are willing to do seemingly anything to make her happy. It’s part of their nature; in fact, when Carol gets really upset or angry, it actually physically harms them. This creates a fascinating tension as she has to regulate her emotions while going through an unimaginably stressful situation. There’s a lot going on, and the first two episodes are mostly about Carol coming to grips with the bizarre situation. Which is good, because it gives viewers time to come to grips with it as well. While Pluribus has some of the energy of a post-apocalyptic story, it’s also completely unlike them in many ways. Because, really, does this world actually need saving? No one in The Walking Dead wants to be a flesh-eating zombie. But turning into a perpetually chipper person? Well, that might not be so bad. As one of the others says early on, the day the change happened was the “greatest day in the history of humanity,” and it’s not impossible to understand why some might agree, even if Carol certainly doesn’t. Pluribus really digs into the nitty-gritty of how this new and very unique world works, and it isn’t afraid to take its time doing so. There’s a level of trust that Gilligan and his team have put into the show’s structure. “The older I get, the more confident I get, not in terms of my abilities but in the wisdom of the audience,” Gilligan told me ahead of the premiere. “The kind of shows that we create attract really smart viewers.” [Image: That’s why there are long, often dialogue-free sequences depicting, say, a woman getting on a plane and flying halfway around the world. You don’t know why she’s doing it at all initially, or even who she is, but the show rewards your patience. The same goes for seemingly boring practical details like how food production works in a world where most of humanity is incapable of harming any living creature. These aspects of the story provide some of the most impactful — and occasionally disturbing — revelations. Pluribus has a strange premise, but the show’s creators also think it through to its logical conclusion (at least that’s true early on; I haven’t seen the whole season yet). This slow drip of reveals and information is absorbing because Pluribus is such a well-executed show. This is especially true when it comes to Seehorn’s performance, which anchors the whole thing. Carol is not a typical heroic character; she’s a miserable and often frustrating character, and yet it’s hard to keep your eyes off of Seehorn, who makes you laugh, cry, and want to wring her neck, often all at the same time. Which means that while those “What the fuck?” moments are common, they’re not frustrating like they can be in similar shows. (Sorry, Lost.) The reveals aren’t gotcha moments. Pluribus isn’t a puzzle box meant to be solved. It’s a story with a lot of strange and complicated things to share with you — and it’s more than comfortable taking its time doing just that. The first two episodes of Pluribus are streaming on Apple TV on November 7th.

articles.title: Spotify’s latest ‘Wrapped’ covers your entire music history
articles.summary: Spotify is celebrating its 20th anniversary by giving listeners a “fully personalized look at their entire music history.”
articles.body: Spotify is celebrating its 20th anniversary by giving listeners a “fully personalized look at their entire music history.” Starting today, Spotify mobile app users can access a new Wrapped-like experience that features “never-before-shared data” going back to when they first joined the service. The “Spotify 20: Your Party of the Year(s)” experience will allow users to look back on their first day on Spotify, the first song they streamed, their most-listened to artist, and the total number of unique songs listened to since creating their account. Spotify is also putting together an All-Time Top Songs Playlist that includes the top 120 tracks a user has listened to, alongside figures showing how many times they have played each song. Spotify doesn’t describe this anniversary experience as an official “Wrapped,” but the format is similar to those annual listening throwbacks — it just goes back much further. And like Wrapped, the “Your Party of the Year(s)” history will also come with a shareable custom stat card that’s designed to be sent to friends or posted on social media. [Image: Here’s an example of some of the stat cards that will be available for users to share. Users can access this new experience by searching for “Spotify 20” or “Party of the Year(s)” within the mobile app, or visiting spotify.com/20 directly on mobile devices. We have asked Spotify if the recap will also be available to desktop users.

articles.title: In a big year for horror, Widow’s Bay still stands apart
articles.summary: With Backrooms and Obsession, 2026 has been a great year for horror, but there’s nothing like Widow’s Bay on Apple TV.
articles.body: Horror is having a moment. In 2026, the genre is especially well-represented: new blood is dominating the box office through films like Backrooms and Obsession, established names like Sam Raimi and Damian McCarthy are at the top of their game, and long-running franchises like 28 Years Later and Resident Evil continue to stay relevant. But the most impressive piece of horror this year might just be found in the world of TV comedy: Widow’s Bay, a series that manages the delicate balance of mixing scares with laughs, while also doubling as a loving tribute to the genre. It’s the kind of combination that often doesn’t work, which is part of what makes the show so remarkable. Widow’s Bay just wrapped up its first season — a second has already been confirmed — and it tells a story that at first sounds incredibly derivative. It takes place on an isolated island in New England, which has a sordid history due to what the locals believe is a curse. In the first episode, a terrifying fog rolls into town, suggesting that a powerful evil is waking up again. Cue the Stephen King comparisons. But it’s not long before Widow’s Bay’s distinct brand of horror / comedy makes itself clear. The show is largely centered on the island’s hapless mayor, Tom (Matthew Rhys), who has a misguided desire to turn Widow’s Bay into a tourist destination that can rival Martha’s Vineyard and Cape Cod. This, of course, runs counter to the whole curse thing. And the incoming fog is just the first sign that things are not going to go well for him and his plan, though Tom ignores the signs at every opportunity. [Image: What makes the show work is that, at its core, it’s just a really scary and tense story. From the very first episode, when Tom is stressing out about a visiting travel writer from The New York Times, there’s a steadily rising sense of dread: a tour through the island’s history that’s full of stories of death and, uh, cannibalism; a calendar about wolves that for some reason also has car crash photos; a ferry captain who says simply “bad things happen here.” The show makes you feel as uneasy as the island’s residents. That sensation only grows over the course of the season, as each episode explores a different horror genre while building on the cursed lore of the island. The second episode takes place in a clearly haunted hotel, complete with a killer clown; later there’s a demonic party planning book that leads to a terrifying and unsettling beach gathering. Tom’s assistant Patricia (Kate O’Flynn) gets hunted by a Jason Voorhees–style slasher villain, and there’s even a darkly inventive take on a drug trip sequence, complete with jarring time skips. It’s because it’s such a well-crafted horror story that the comedy in Widow’s Bay hits so hard. It’s not the easiest genre mix to pull off, as creator and showrunner Katie Dippold — who knows a thing about how funny horror can be — told me ahead of the show’s premiere in April. “It can be a great combo, but it can also be a bad combo,” she explained, noting that projects that successfully blend the two genres are “few and far between.” As if to prove her point, the new Scary Movie released this month was entirely toothless. But unlike more overt attempts at infusing horror with comedy, most of the gags in Widow’s Bay are comparatively subtle — and scary in their own way. When Tom is looking through a collection of board games at the local inn, he finds one simply called Teeth; inside, there’s nothing but a pair of pliers. When Patricia finally kills the “boogeyman” who has been stalking her, she keeps her shotgun trained on his corpse at all times — from the ambulance to cremation — just in case. Even the episode titles can be hilarious. The finale, where just about everything goes wrong, is called “We hope you enjoyed your time!” [Image: This means that the jokes not only fit into the eerie nature of the world, they actually heighten it. And that was the goal all along. “I never wanted to have a moment where something scary happens and the characters don’t react truthfully,” Dippold told me. “If you’re truthful, then eventually you’ll find the comedy. That was the very hard rule.” This all comes to a head as the show wrapped up its first season. Leading into the finale, Tom was put in an impossible situation, forced to choose whether to kill his adorably inept secretary Ruth (K Callan) in order to end the curse for good, or doom the island by not acting. In the last episode, with the town’s residents and tourists stuck in a shelter due to a destructive storm, Tom finds himself in Ruth’s house, and it’s genuinely painful watching him try to decide the right path. But amidst all of this tension, there are still funny bits, like Ruth casually noting that an old boyfriend “got bit by an animal and became that animal,” or a cheerful instructional video on ritual sacrifice. And this being Widow’s Bay, things are a bit more complex than they appear, leaving Tom with an even more difficult task in front of him. You don’t just have to take my word for it. Guillermo del Toro recently called the series “hands down one of the most mesmerizing acts of narrative prestidigitation in horror.” That’s some high praise. But so is the fact that Widow’s Bay has managed to claim its own distinct lane in such a crowded moment. The finale title turned out to be incredibly accurate: I did, in fact, enjoy my time. The first season of Widow’s Bay is streaming now on Apple TV.

articles.title: At 28, Amitabh Bachchan’s granddaughter Navya Naveli Nanda works with father Nikhil Nanda at Rs 32,500-cr Escorts Kubota; says 'I would never want to restrict my identity' beyond Bachchan-Nanda legacy
articles.summary: At 28, Navya Naveli Nanda's corporate journey began in an environment far removed from the usual image associated with her famous family - around trac.
articles.body: At 28, Navya Naveli Nanda's corporate journey began in an environment far removed from the usual image associated with her famous family - around tractors and heavy farm machinery. Today, the entrepreneur works closely alongside her father, Nikhil Nanda, Chairman and Managing Director of Escorts Kubota, the listed tractor and engineering company with a market value of roughly Rs 32,500 crore.But Navya Naveli Nanda is determined to carve out an identity beyond the Bachchan-Nanda surname. The entrepreneur, who is the daughter of Shweta Bachchan Nanda and Nikhil Nanda and granddaughter of Amitabh Bachchan and Jaya Bachchan, has been vocal about building a career and life defined by her own work.Navya Naveli Nanda on Gen ZSpeaking at the launch of Aparajita, the Hindi edition of former State Bank of India Chairperson Arundhati Bhattacharya's memoir Indomitable, Navya discussed the changing priorities of Gen Z.“Young people don’t just want profit; they want purpose,” she said, describing what she sees as a strong desire among her generation to contribute to society, women and themselves.Bhattacharya, who was also part of the conversation, dismissed the stereotype that Gen Z is entitled or unwilling to work, calling the perception “totally wrong.”Navya on the uncertainty surrounding AINavya did not claim that her generation has faced greater hardships than previous generations. Instead, she said technology has eliminated some of the challenges that earlier generations experienced, while creating new uncertainties of its own.One of the biggest concerns, she noted, is artificial intelligence and its potential impact on jobs and careers.Despite those uncertainties, Nanda believes Gen Z is developing resilience through a stronger sense of purpose. She described the commitment among young people to contributing to society as “very, very strong”.Navya Naveli Nanda on women's equalityThe entrepreneur also spoke about gender equality and how young people increasingly view men and women as equals.According to Nanda, seeing the person across the table as an equal gives young women greater confidence to express their opinions. However, she acknowledged that stereotypes and structural barriers continue to exist.For her, gender equality should not simply mean women trying to catch up with men.“I think it’s about creating our own blueprint,” she said, referring to how women should be able to decide how they want to live and contribute.Nanda also stressed that men have an important role to play as partners, fathers and brothers in creating a more equal society.Navya Naveli Nanda on her famous surnameThe question of identity is particularly personal for Navya, who comes from two prominent Indian families.Her maternal grandparents are Amitabh Bachchan and Jaya Bachchan, while her paternal grandparents were the late industrialist Rajan Nanda and entrepreneur Ritu Nanda. Her father, Nikhil Nanda, heads Escorts Kubota, while her mother, Shweta Bachchan Nanda, is a writer and entrepreneur.During the conversation, Navya was asked how she separates her own identity from the surname she was born into and whether the legacy comes with additional pressure.Navya acknowledged the responsibility that comes with having a prominent family name.“Everyone has a surname,” she said, adding that she believes everyone has an equal responsibility to live up to that name.At the same time, she made it clear that she does not want her identity to be defined solely by her family.“I would never want to restrict my identity to just my last name,” she said, adding that she does not want to be defined only by her roles as a daughter, granddaughter, sister or friend.She said women are “far beyond those labels” and expressed her desire to build an identity through both her professional and personal life.Ritu Nanda's influence on Navya's careerAmong the women who influenced Navya's ambitions, her late grandmother Ritu Nanda holds a particularly significant place.Ritu Nanda, the eldest daughter of legendary filmmaker and actor Raj Kapoor, was an entrepreneur and businesswoman. Navya recalled growing up around her grandmother's business life and being fascinated by the excitement with which she spoke about her work.While friends would sometimes tease Navya for being so interested in business, she said her grandmother's enthusiasm made the corporate world seem like “the most exciting place imaginable.”“A lot of my dadi's ambition, a lot of her strength, a lot of what she did when she was younger and what I saw growing up,” Navya said, “has led me to be sitting here on this stage sharing that with you today.”She also credited her mother, Shweta Bachchan Nanda, and grandmother Jaya Bachchan as important role models while growing up.Navya Naveli Nanda's work beyond the family businessWhile Navya works alongside her father at Escorts Kubota, her professional interests extend beyond the family business.She co-founded Aara Health, a women-focused health and wellness platform, and founded Project Naveli, a non-profit initiative focused on gender equality and creating opportunities for women.She is also co-authoring The Map, a forthcoming book from HarperCollins India that explores and challenges stereotypes surrounding Gen Z.For Nanda, the question is not whether she can escape the legacy she was born into, but how she can build something of her own while acknowledging where she comes from.“I think what has been passed around me is far more than what I might even achieve in my life,” she said.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 1985, Mithun Chakraborty bought this sprawling Madh Island bungalow; the lavish house has separate cottages for family members
articles.summary: Bollywood star Mithun Chakraborty has built a remarkable career after facing severe financial struggles during his early years in Mumbai. The actor, w.
articles.body: Bollywood star Mithun Chakraborty has built a remarkable career after facing severe financial struggles during his early years in Mumbai. The actor, who entered the film industry with limited means, eventually became one of the biggest stars of his generation.His debut film also earned him a National Award. Yet, Mithun Chakraborty's early days were far removed from the comfortable life he leads today. The actor has spoken about sleeping on the streets and cleaning an office to gain access to its washroom. He had also once requested an interviewer to feed him. Today, Mithun Chakraborty owns several properties across India. Among his most distinctive residences is his sprawling bungalow at Madh Island in Mumbai. The property covers nearly 1.5 acres, which is around 65,000 sq ft.In 1985, Mithun Chakraborty bought his Madh Island bungalowThe property has been part of Mithun Chakraborty's family for several decades. His younger son, Namashi Chakraborty, recently spoke about the sprawling residence and its history during a conversation with Pinkvilla. “My parents bought this house in 1985, a few months after my elder brother Mimoh was born,” Namashi Chakraborty said. The family did not immediately make the Mumbai property their permanent home. They later moved to Ooty and continued living there until 2007. After returning to Mumbai, the family began staying at the Madh Island bungalow full-time. Before that transition, the property was primarily used as a holiday home. The sprawling premises now have plenty of greenery and space for the family's 22 dogs. Gardening is also one of Mithun Chakraborty's interests. “Dad loves gardening. He often keeps himself busy doing that,” Namashi Chakraborty said.The property has separate cottages for family membersRather than housing everyone inside a single structure, the bungalow has been divided into multiple cottages. Each one serves a specific purpose or provides space for different members of the family. “There are different cottages for different family members. Both my father and grandfather believed that every kid should have their own space,” Namashi Chakraborty explained. One cottage has been converted into a gym. Another is used to accommodate guests. The cottage opposite the guest area is used by Mithun Chakraborty and his wife whenever they are in Mumbai. Another cottage functions as an office. It is also where professional conversations related to the family's film projects take place. “Dad mostly stays in Kolkata”, revealed Namashi Chakraborty. "All the film-related talks as well as script discussions happen in this office,” Namashi Chakraborty said.Mithun Chakraborty's office preserves his legacyThe office is more than just a workspace. It also contains several reminders of Mithun Chakraborty's decades-long career in cinema. One wall displays his awards, along with paintings and sketches created by fans. Other sections feature photographs of Mithun Chakraborty with prominent personalities from different stages of his life. The collection includes pictures with Kannada cinema legend Rajkumar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Bal Thackeray. There is also a photograph capturing Mithun Chakraborty receiving the Dadasaheb Phalke Award. The property has also hosted several celebrity gatherings over the years. Its courtyard reportedly became a celebration space during the family's Diwali parties. Actors such as Dharmendra and Jeetendra have been among the guests at these celebrations.Mithun Chakraborty's sons have an in-house studioThe Madh Island residence has also evolved into a creative space for the next generation of the family. A separate cottage has been transformed into a full-fledged studio. Mithun Chakraborty's sons use the facility for filmmaking activities. They can also create different sets within the property. The arrangement allows the family to conduct several film-related activities without leaving the sprawling premises.Mithun Chakraborty's yellow Beetle was once his 'first home'Among the most unusual objects associated with the property is a yellow Volkswagen Beetle. Namashi Chakraborty described the vehicle as his father's first home in Mumbai. The car dates back to Mithun Chakraborty's difficult early period. Although it is no longer fit to be driven, the actor continues to spend money on maintaining it. “When dad came to Mumbai, he didn’t have a house to live. He spent 15 days of his life in this yellow Beetle. This was his first house. Now, it is not in a condition to be driven, yet dad spends a lot of money in its maintenance,” Namashi revealed. Namashi did not disclose how Mithun Chakraborty gained access to the vehicle during those initial days. articles.title: In 2020, Zac Efron invested money in a bushland; six years later, he is turning it into his sustainable and eco-friendly hemp home
articles.summary: Zac Efron is transforming 311 acres of bushland in New South Wales into a sustainable eco-friendly home made of hemp and biodegradable materials, collaborating with designer Joost Bakker for a green future.
articles.body: Zac Efron has been looking for a space to build a unique and sustainable version of his home, which he found in the bushlands of New South Wales. The property, located an hour from Byron Bay and spanning 311 acres, is supposed to be made entirely of hemp and other biodegradable materials found in nature. The actor, who rose to popularity for his leading role in ‘High School Musical,' has invested significant time, energy, and money into his passion project to build his own off-grid, eco-friendly dream home.Zac Efron bought the barren bushlands in 2020Australian Financial Review reported that the 38-year-old star purchased the large piece of land in New South Wales six years ago. He had invested in the bushlands to create his dream project; however, getting it off the ground took some time. Now, he is working on creating his ‘FutureCave’ with the help of the innovative Dutch-Australian designer Joost Bakker.Using internal bricks and joinery, Efron and Bakker are planning on making the entire home out of hemp. The product is stated to be sourced from a farm that is located somewhere in southern New South Wales. Not only the building itself, but a lot of the items within the home itself will be made with the use of hemp, one way or the other, including mattresses, curtains, pillows, and other similar items.The remainder of the home is also going to be made using similar natural items. According to another report shared online by Realtor.com, the project will use constructed hemp blocks, recycled oyster shells, agricultural waste, and sustainable particle boards. Efron is going all out with Bakker in planning this home, seeing as the land had been sitting there barren since he first purchased it for an undisclosed amount in 2020.Joost Bakker is quite excited to work on Zac Efron’s homeIn November last year, Bakker had taken to his Instagram and posted about how Zac Efron had asked him to work on the home and how big of an honour it all was for him. He had shared a photo of the two and wrote in the caption: “For the past year we've experimented with making hemp blocks, replacing concrete with two materials that restore the environment: hemp, possibly the best plant on earth at repairing and restoring soil health, and, of course, oysters, nature's ultimate ocean restorer. We are using the most cutting-edge technology (invented by the Romans 2000+ years ago). I want to create a building material that I hope will become mainstream one day—a material that naturally breathes, is anti-mould, is naturally fire-resistant, and improves the indoor air Zac will ultimately breathe. Big thank you to the Rennie family in Hillston, NSW, who have supported this project with their hemp (and ideas!). We are getting close now, @agrico_hillston. Also, shout-out to @shuckdontchuck. I'll keep you posted on how these blocks turn out.”Since then, he has been regularly sharing updates on his account about the project and working with Efron. In May, earlier this year, he shared that he is about to start work on his home. He wrote, "Excited to get started on Zac’s house! Especially want to thank these two legends, @main__frank, for working so hard to get this project designed and approved!”His latest update came in July, when he shared a photo with the actor, possibly in his factory or working studio, as everyone was seen wearing safety goggles and orange jackets. He wrote, “Grant Shelton from @forest1au has worked in this factory for 35 years, gaining an immeasurable amount of knowledge and skills. Turning the by-product from the sawmill on site into particle board. He and his team have used this experience to turn a crop that takes 3-4 months to harvest from a seed into an exceptional quality particle board.” He also mentioned that hemp has a lot of abilities to rejuvenate the soil and that they are excited for this project to take off.More details about Zac Efron’s homeThe outlet further shared that Efron’s home will have something called six "bedroom pods." All of the structures are going to be connected by an outdoor walkway and will also boast their own personal bathroom area, along with a rooftop garden. Efron is also planning on building a large living area on the property as well.Efron also sat down for an interview with the outlet, talking about how and why he wanted to create something like this. He shared, “I live a pretty fast-paced life and work quite a bit, so in between movies and press tours, my number one goal is always to take time for myself and rest and recharge and to be in nature as much as possible and as close to the earth as I can, and this land just feels like it's perfect for that.”In 2021, Efron also put his famous LA home on the market and has been planning on fully shifting to Australia.Zac Efron last appeared in films with ‘A Family Affair’ in 2024. He currently has two films lined up for release; however, the dates have not yet been confirmed. articles.title: Mom-to-be Samantha Ruth Prabhu shares traditional baby shower pictures with hubby Raj Nidimoru; says, ‘I have always had a deep respect for our traditions’
articles.summary: Samantha Ruth Prabhu, who is expecting her first child with her husband and filmmaker Raj Nidimoru, recently gave fans a glimpse into her traditional .
articles.body: Samantha Ruth Prabhu, who is expecting her first child with her husband and filmmaker Raj Nidimoru, recently gave fans a glimpse into her traditional baby shower celebration on Monday, coinciding with Ganesh Chaturthi. The actress shared a couple of dreamy pictures from the ceremony, expressing her respect for and belief in “traditions passed down through generations.”Samantha Ruth Prabhu shares baby shower picturesSamantha Ruth Prabhu took to her Instagram handle to share pictures in which she can be seen looking beautiful in a yellow ethnic outfit, with her hair left open and minimal makeup.Speaking of her accessories, the actress chose a silver choker necklace, along with matching earrings and bangles. The pictures gave fans a glimpse of the special celebrations as Samantha and her family marked the occasion with traditional rituals.Samantha Ruth Prabhu talks about her love for traditionsThe ‘Maa Inti Bangaaram’ star also talked about her deep respect for Indian traditions and rituals. She said that while she may not understand the meaning behind every ritual, she believes there is something deeper connected to them.Her caption read, “I have always had a deep respect for our traditions. I may not understand the meaning behind every ritual, but I have always believed that there is something deeper at work... in the sound of a mantra, the energy created through chanting, and the careful way the ancient practices have been passed down through generations.”Raj Nidimoru and their family attend the celebrationSamantha’s filmmaker husband, Raj Nidimoru, was also seen taking part in the festivities. Other family members were present during the traditional ceremony as well.Ram Charan’s wife, Upasana Kamineni Konidela, reacted to the pictures and wrote, “So lovely.” Actress Krithi Shetty also dropped a red heart emoji in the comments section.For the unversed, Samantha confirmed her pregnancy during the success meet of her latest release, ‘Maa Inti Bangaaram’. The actress also revealed that she would take a maternity break after the film. The film went on to cross Rs 100 crore worldwide upon its theatrical release.Samantha Ruth Prabhu and Raj Nidimoru are said to have met for the first time during the shoot of ‘The Family Man’ Season 2. They later worked together on ‘Citadel: Honey Bunny’.Samantha tied the knot with Raj Nidimoru in December 2025.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body:

articles.title: Eric Lahuerta, cocinero: "El truco para que las patatas bravas queden crujientes por fuera y cremosas por dentro está en la temperatura del aceite"
articles.standfirst: El chef explica cómo hacer unas patatas bravas caseras perfectas con una doble fritura y el aceite a 180 grados
articles.summary: El chef explica cómo hacer unas patatas bravas caseras perfectas con una doble fritura y el aceite a 180 grados
articles.body: Las patatas bravas son uno de los grandes clásicos de la gastronomía española, pero conseguir que queden crujientes por fuera y tiernas por dentro no depende únicamente de elegir una buena patata. La temperatura del aceite y la forma de realizar la fritura son dos de los factores que pueden marcar la diferencia entre una tapa bien hecha y unas patatas blandas o excesivamente grasas. El chef y creador de contenido Eric Lahuerta ha explicado su método para preparar unas patatas bravas caseras con una textura crujiente en el exterior y cremosa en el interior. Su principal consejo pasa por realizar una doble fritura en el mismo aceite, comenzando a baja temperatura y terminando a fuego fuerte. "El truco para conseguir unas patatas bravas crujientes por fuera y cremosas por dentro está en la temperatura del aceite", explica Lahuerta. El primer paso consiste en cortar las patatas en dados. El cocinero recomienda utilizar una variedad blanca o monalisa y, antes de llevarlas a la sartén, introducirlas en un recipiente con agua fría para eliminar parte del almidón. Este paso ayuda a evitar que las patatas se peguen entre sí durante la fritura. Después llega uno de los puntos más importantes de la técnica. Lahuerta aconseja utilizar una sartén antiadherente con aceite de oliva virgen extra y colocar las patatas directamente cuando el aceite todavía está frío. "Enciende el fuego y déjalo a fuego medio. Y directamente con el aceite en frío, añade todas las patatas", explica. La idea es que las patatas se vayan cocinando poco a poco mientras el aceite aumenta de temperatura. De esta forma, el interior se cocina antes de buscar el dorado del exterior. El momento decisivo llega cuando el aceite alcanza los 180 grados. Según el chef, entonces hay que aumentar la potencia del fuego para terminar de freír las patatas y conseguir que adquieran ese aspecto dorado y una textura crujiente. "La patata se va cocinando y en el interior va quedando bien tierna. Cuando el aceite llegue a 180 grados, va a terminar de freír la patata, dándole ese color dorado", explica. El procedimiento consiste, por tanto, en dos fases diferenciadas: primero se pochan las patatas a baja temperatura y después se fríen a fuego fuerte. "Lo que hacemos es una doble fritura en el mismo aceite. Primero, pochamos a baja temperatura, y después, freímos a fuego fuerte", señala Lahuerta. La patata es solo una parte de la receta. Para Lahuerta, la salsa también resulta fundamental para conseguir unas buenas bravas. Su preparación comienza con cebolla cortada en juliana, ajo y cayena, que deben cocinarse hasta que la cebolla quede bien caramelizada. Después incorpora un hueso de jamón y tomate cortado en dados. El hueso sirve para potenciar el sabor del sofrito. A continuación se añade un buen chorro de vino blanco y se deja reducir completamente. Cuando el vino ha reducido, el cocinero recomienda incorporar una cucharada de pimentón dulce y media de pimentón picante. El último paso consiste en añadir caldo de pollo y dejar que la mezcla cocine entre 10 y 15 minutos, hasta que el líquido reduzca y la preparación adquiera textura de salsa. Después se tritura hasta conseguir una salsa fina.

articles.title: Ester Expósito rompe su silencio y habla por primera vez de la polémica con el Xokas: "No tuve que hacer nada"
articles.standfirst: La actriz cuenta a María Guerra cómo vivió los comentarios del streamer y celebra la reacción de Burger King tras la polémica
articles.summary: La actriz cuenta a María Guerra cómo vivió los comentarios del streamer y celebra la reacción de Burger King tras la polémica
articles.body: Ester Expósito se ha pronunciado por primera vez sobre la polémica que protagonizó junto a El Xokas este verano. La actriz ha hablado con María Guerra en La Script en una entrevista en la que ha explicado cómo vivió las reacciones a los comentarios del streamer y qué conclusión sacó de todo lo ocurrido. La conversación llega después de que las declaraciones de El Xokas sobre Expósito provocaran una fuerte controversia y de que Burger King decidiera posteriormente cancelar su colaboración con el creador de contenido. El episodio comenzó cuando El Xokas habló de la actriz durante una retransmisión y aseguró que, aunque le parecía un "diez", no estaría con una mujer como ella por sus ideas políticas y que preferiría estar con una que fuera "un seis". Sus palabras generaron numerosas críticas y la polémica llegó incluso al Congreso de los Diputados. Ahora, meses después, María Guerra preguntó directamente a Expósito cómo había gestionado aquella situación. La periodista fue quien hizo referencia a las palabras del streamer y a la imagen que se había generado alrededor de ellas. La respuesta de la actriz fue clara: considera que no necesitó intervenir porque, a su juicio, las propias imágenes y declaraciones hablaban por sí solas. "No tuve que hacer nada. La situación era tan... hablaba por sí sola, la imagen, lo que decía", explica Expósito durante la entrevista. La actriz añade que para ella fue "maravilloso" que se produjera una situación en la que no tuviera que salir públicamente a responder. Más allá de las declaraciones concretas del streamer, Expósito asegura que lo que más le sorprendió de todo el episodio fue la reacción que recibió por parte de otras personas. La actriz explica que habitualmente percibe en las redes sociales mucho ruido procedente del odio, el extremismo y los comentarios misóginos. Por eso, encontrarse con una reacción diferente le sirvió para recordar que también existe otra parte de la sociedad que permanece más silenciosa. En ese momento, según cuenta, recordó que también hay "gente con dos dedos de frente" que no es misógina ni está "llena de odio, de veneno". Y considera que esa parte de la sociedad simplemente suele hacer menos ruido. "Esta gente está ahí, lo que pasa es que normalmente están calladas, tranquilas con sus vidas y los que hacen más ruido son los otros", señala. Durante la conversación con María Guerra también aparece la decisión de Burger King de poner fin a su colaboración con El Xokas. La cadena anunció el 16 de julio que cancelaba la colaboración con el creador de contenido y aseguró que sus declaraciones no representaban los valores que defendía la compañía. Sin embargo, la actriz introduce una reflexión más amplia sobre el caso. Para ella, el problema no termina con una polémica concreta ni con la reacción de una marca. "Él me puso a mí, yo era la diana en ese caso de sus declaraciones, pero ¿cuántas cosas no habrá dicho antes esta persona y tantas como él, y ahí siguen y no pasa nada? Y tienen a muchísimos oyentes y a gente que piensa como ellos", plantea. Expósito considera que habría que actuar antes cuando personas con grandes audiencias realizan este tipo de declaraciones, especialmente cuando sus mensajes pueden llegar a millones de seguidores. "A lo mejor hay que actuar antes", concluye.

articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Lady Gaga: ‘You have a much greater mission on this earth...Your mission is to give people a form of love through your art that lifts them up,’ a powerful life lesson on kindness, purpose and inspiring others
articles.summary: Discover Lady Gaga's inspiring quote about the deeper mission of artists to spread love and kindness through their art. Explore her transformation and thoughts on creativity in today's social media age.
articles.body: Lady Gaga has always done things her own way. Her clothes, music and stage performances have helped make her instantly recognisable. But there is another side to the singer that goes beyond the costumes and the attention they receive. Gaga has often spoken about her work, her fans and the kind of feeling she wants her art to leave behind.As her career moved forward, her thoughts about fame changed too. Earlier, getting a reaction was often part of her image. Later, she began talking more about kindness and what her music could offer to someone listening. For Gaga, being an artist is not only about being noticed; it is also about having something meaningful to say. It is also about making someone feel better, stronger or less alone.Today's quote of the day by Lady Gaga reads: "You have a much greater mission on this earth than to freak the hell out of people. Your mission is to give people a form of love through your art that lifts them up."What does the quote by Lady Gaga mean?Lady Gaga offered these words in a 2019 interview with ELLE. Those experiences made her look past the shock value that had once been attached to her image.The main takeaway from Gaga’s words is simple: an audience has a responsibility. An artist can use that attention merely to entertain or can use it to leave people with something meaningful.The phrase "lifts them up," is equally important. Gaga is talking about work that leaves an audience feeling encouraged rather than diminished. Her thoughts during the interview also reflected her growing belief in kindness and the positive use of her influence.How is the quote by Lady Gaga relevant today?The thought becomes even more interesting in the age of social media. Today, attention can arrive within seconds, but keeping that attention often means competing with thousands of other voices. Controversial opinions, dramatic content and outrage can quickly become viral.For young creators, that environment can make it tempting to believe that the loudest content is always the most successful. Gaga's words suggest another possibility: creativity does not have to shock people to matter.A song might help someone get through a difficult day. A movie can make a person see their own experiences differently. A photograph, story or social media post can remind someone that their feelings are understood.That is why her words can extend beyond the entertainment industry. Students, writers, teachers, influencers and professionals also have an audience in their own spaces. What they choose to say can affect the people listening to them.Early life of Lady GagaBorn Stefani Joanne Angelina Germanotta on March 28, 1986, in New York City, Gaga showed an interest in music from a young age. Gaga took up the piano at the age of four and started writing music while she was still young. She later enrolled at New York University's Tisch School of the Arts, but decided to leave after a year and concentrate on becoming a musician. She spent the next few years performing at venues in New York and trying out different sounds and looks. It was also when she started developing the stage persona that would become known as Lady Gaga.Lady Gaga’s rise to fame'The Fame' was released in 2008 and Gaga’s name began to spread to a much wider audience. 'Just Dance' and 'Poker Face' became early favourites and helped establish her in the pop music scene. Her unusual visual style and theatrical performances made her instantly recognisable, while her music established her as one of pop's major new voices.She continued that success with The Fame Monster in 2009, which included songs such as 'Bad Romance' and 'Telephone'. Her career expanded further with albums including Born This Way, as she continued experimenting with her sound and public image.Music was eventually joined by acting. Gaga played Ally in 'A Star Is Born' with Bradley Cooper. The role brought her acting work into the spotlight, while 'Shallow' took home the Academy Award for Best Original Song.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 2006, Rowan Atkinson spent GBP 2.6 million to create his own glass mansion; 16 years later, the actor finally came back home
articles.summary: After investing GBP 2.6 million in a 1930s property, Rowan Atkinson finally completed his futuristic glass mansion, a project plagued by delays and local opposition, after 16 years of planning and construction.
articles.body: Almost 20 years ago, ‘Mr Bean’ star Rowan Atkinson invested a whopping GBP 2.6 million into a 1930s home located in Ipsden, Oxfordshire. However, the actor planned to demolish the property to start work on his futuristic glass mansion spanning 16 acres of land. The old property, known as the Handsmooth House, had been there for decades before Atkinson took ownership for his dream project. However, while building his new home, the veteran icon faced many issues. Here is a look at how it took 16 years to get Atkinson’s home off the ground and ready for him to move in.Rowan Atkinson bought a 1930s property with 16 acres of land for a glass mansionAt the time, Atkinson had bought the property with his now ex-wife, Sunetra Sastry, with whom he filed for divorce in 2015. Daily Express reported that the actor wanted to make changes to the initial property, even though it was well equipped and had its own private garage space, among other amenities. The star still had the main house torn down to install his 8,000-square-foot home made from glass and metal.The home that took 16 years to buildHe took the help of American architect Richard Meier, who created Atkinson’s vision into a reality, and further installed a guest pavilion and a tennis court on the 16 acres of land along with the large main house. Although he had bought the property for GBP 2.6 million, over the years he invested around GBP 5 million to get the entire thing made according to his taste. Renovations were extensive, and the house faced many issues over the years, including permission problems and unhappy neighbours. This all affected the process, and the home took around 16 years to complete.Rowan Atkinson’s neighbours were not happy with the homeHowever, the process was not easy, and the actor’s neighbours in the area were not at all happy with his choices. The Oxford Mail reported at the time that they believed the home did not suit the aesthetics of the area. They called it a "space-age petrol station" and even applied for his application for the home to be rejected by the South Oxfordshire Council. In another report shared online by the BBC, during a planning meeting, Atkinson admitted that the house did not sit well with the backdrop of the area and instead stood out; however, he stated that this reason was not enough to block his project. His consultant also stated at the time, “The home will add to our architectural heritage rather than parody it.” The locals actively opposed the building, with one local stating, “Money and fame have been used to bulldoze their way through the planning process." The decision on this monstrosity is outrageous and sets a very dangerous precedent. A few neighbours, according to the outlets, also wrote notes supporting the actor and found no issues with the structure. After much contemplation, the council later granted his request to build his glass mansion.In 2016, the star properly started construction of his home, with photos shared online by The Mirror showing the building mid-construction in the area. By 2022, the renovations were completed, and the actor officially came back home and moved back in with his long-time partner, actress Louise Ford, and their daughter.The property is now covered in white paint, features its own tennis court, private garage area, and a serene Japanese garden area that the Atkinson family often spends their time in.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Tanishaa Mukerji has sparked a debate on X after sharing her views on women who have relationships with married men. The actress described such women .
articles.body: Tanishaa Mukerji has sparked a debate on X after sharing her views on women who have relationships with married men. The actress described such women as “evil” and argued that they cannot be considered feminists, while also holding the married man accountable for his actions.Her post triggered mixed reactions on social media, with some users agreeing with her stance on boundaries and infidelity, while others criticised her for what they viewed asplacing greater blame on the woman involved.What Tanishaa Mukerji said about women dating married menTaking to X, Tanishaa shared her thoughts on relationships involving married people and wrote, “My thoughts – women who have affairs with married men are not feminists. In fact, they are against women! Because being with someone’s husband is disrespecting the wife. The man is to blame too. He lacks character! And women who chase married men are just evil! They should not be role models to our children! #feminist #genz I said what I said! #boundaries (sic).”The actress’s comments quickly attracted attention, with the discussion extending beyond infidelity to questions about feminism, personal boundaries and accountability in relationships.Journalist Richa Lakhera challenges Tanishaa’s argumentWhile some social media users supported Tanishaa’s position, journalist Richa Lakhera disagreed with the actress and questioned the difference in the language she used to describe the man and the woman involved.Responding to Tanishaa’s post, Lakhera wrote, “So ‘lacking character’ is the worst you’ve got for him, but she’s ‘evil’ and unfit to be a role model. The girl made no vow. She broke no promise. The husband’s the one who stood at an altar, said the words, and then went and broke them. That’s not ‘lacking character’; that’s real betrayal. Full stop.”Lakhera further argued that the responsibility for upholding marital vows lies with the person who made them. She wrote, “Calling the other woman ‘evil’ while letting the vow-breaker off with a soft little ‘he’s not perfect either’ isn’t a boundary. It’s a script that says men ‘get weak’ and women get to be villains. The one who owed loyalty and threw it away is the one who did the disrespecting. Say that with the same energy.”About Tanishaa Mukerji’s workTanishaa Mukerji has appeared in films including ‘Neal ‘n’ Nikki’, ‘Sarkar’ and ‘Code Name Abdul’. articles.title: At the 2026 Emmys, wins from Apple TV and Stephen Colbert highlight TV in transition
articles.summary: From Mariska Hargitay’s lighthearted bits to tributes to Dolly Parton and Rob Reiner, this year’s Emmys were heartfelt and memorable. Apple TV was the big winner of the night.
articles.body: Maybe it was watching Stephen Colbert get his final two “Late Show” Emmys engraved at the afterparty. Or hearing the rowdy Apple TV contingent in the audience whoop it up every time “Widow’s Bay” notched another win. But inside the Peacock Theater on Monday night, this year’s Emmy Awards felt like a transition to a new era of television. As the TV Academy’s events crew rolled away the blue carpet, the event gave us plenty of moments to remember. Here are just a few… A host with assists With an opening musical number starring Knicks point guard Jalen Brunson and a “Law & Order: SVU” skit starring Taylor Swift, host Mariska Hargitay called in plenty of favors from her famous friends to help lend the Emmys a little star power. Hargitay, the show’s first female host in 15 years, rotated through at least 10 wardrobe changes, including a “Game of Thrones”-style fur cape and black power suit. But the uniform she kept on all night was cheerleader for the medium of television, going so far as to repurpose a line from Nicole Kidman’s viral AMC Theatres commercial to say, “At the end of the day, we come to TV for magic.” Some of the biggest laughs of the night came from the mini monologue John Mulaney delivered while presenting the category of outstanding lead actor in a drama. “This award is for the guys, just men being men,” Mulaney said. “Finally, something for the fellas.” The award itself wasn’t a surprise — front-runner Noah Wyle of “The Pitt” took it home. But Mulaney’s bit, including a joke that earned a bleep from NBC censors, had the audience in the room roaring and people at home wondering how long until the comic finally hosts a major awards show. (Mulaney did host the Film Academy’s Governors Awards in 2024, but that show isn’t televised). The era of Apple New Apple CEO John Ternus attended the Emmys, and he had lots to celebrate besides the $2,000 foldable iPhone he showed off on the red carpet. For the first time since the tech giant’s streaming service launched in 2019, Apple TV collected more Emmys than any other outlet. Including its wins at last weekend’s two Emmy nights, Apple took home 28 trophies total this year, with a record-setting 14 coming for freshman comedy “Widow’s Bay” and six for “Pluribus.” HBO came in second with 21, with “DTF St Louis” collecting seven and “The Pitt” six. Netflix followed in third with 16, winning three apiece for “Love on the Spectrum” and “Beef.” Quiet reflection over fiery politics If you were betting on Colbert to riff on President Donald Trump and the Federal Communications Commission or open up about the events leading up to his late-night program’s cancellation, you were out of luck. The veteran comedian kept his acceptance speech focused squarely on his gratitude for his 11-year run at CBS, his writing staff and his wife. In general, the Emmys were light on topical humor or references to current events such as the Iran war, AI or the looming Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger. Sally Field did sneak in a subtle line that some interpreted as an anti-merger dig while accepting an Emmy for her performance in the Netflix movie “Remarkably Bright Creatures.” “We’re the arts,” Field said. “We matter. Our voices matter. Our diversity, our unique storytelling matters. We can’t let those voices be silenced, or compromised or merged.” Instead of fiery political commentary, this year’s ceremony leaned more reflective, with earnest meditations from Hargitay and “Pluribus” creator Vince Gilligan on TV’s power to unite a divided country. The winner of one of the night’s marquee categories trained his attention on TV’s important role in troubled times. “Yes, we are entertainers. We make you laugh, we make you cry, occasionally we make you look away in disgust,” R. Scott Gemmill, the creator of “The Pitt,” said in his acceptance speech for best drama series. “But when I look around this room, I see something more important than the awards and the ratings. I see a whole community that is still trying to do the right thing.” Serious notes In a year filled with losses in the entertainment industry, the telecast included sorrowful tributes to the late Rob Reiner, Catherine O’Hara and sitcom giant James Burrows. Reba McEntire sang Dolly Parton’s “Appalachian Memories” just a few weeks after the country music giant’s death, and Noah Kahan performed “Bridge Over Troubled Water” during the In Memoriam montage. But the longest ovation of the night came for a performer who has defied the odds to remain in the business: Michael J. Fox, accepting the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award from his wheelchair. Fox shared that he kept his Parkinson’s diagnosis secret for a long time and wondered if audiences would still laugh at his jokes if they knew he was sick. Ultimately, he said, “I understood that accepting Parkinson’s didn’t mean I had to surrender to it.” The two Emmys personas For years, Jack Nicholson appeared in the front row at the Oscars, the picture of cool detachment and old Hollywood charm. “Shrinking” nominee Harrison Ford seems to be stepping into that role at the Emmys, as the guy everyone else seems to want to get next to, who really himself just wants to get home. In contrast Monday night was enthusiastic “Widow’s Bay” creator Katie Dippold, who didn’t even try to contain her glee at her show’s many awards. During her acceptance speech for writing, Dippold declared, “I promise all of you that no one will ever step foot in my home without seeing this thing (her Emmy). I’m sorry, this is going to become my entire personality now.”

articles.title: Quote of the day for children by Meghan Markle: ‘We just need to be kinder to ourselves. If we treated ourselves the way we treated our best friend, can you imagine how much better off we would be?’ The ‘Suits’ star’s lesson on qualities a child should have
articles.summary: In her powerful message, Meghan Markle encourages children to treat themselves with the same kindness they offer their best friends, promoting self-compassion and better mental well-being.
articles.body: Meghan Markle has been an inspirational voice over the past couple of years, working with organizations and charities to raise money and awareness for many causes. Today’s quote of the day from the ‘Suits’ actress is specifically something that children need to keep in mind at all times. Building on your self-worth and self-awareness is an important quality that everyone needs to work on from a young age.The quote of the day for children from Meghan Markle reads, "We just need to be kinder to ourselves. If we treated ourselves the way we treated our best friend, can you imagine how much better off we would be?”What does the quote mean?Meghan Markle shared these words during an interview with AOL Build in March 2016. During the interview, the ‘Suits’ star discussed themes of self-care, confidence, and women's empowerment.Markle’s quote is all about self-compassion and shifting your inner dialogue. She compares how we would treat a friend to how we treat ourselves, opening the conversation to what would happen if we started treating ourselves with the same amount of respect, love, and consideration.For example, when a close friend or someone we love makes a mistake, fails a test, or goes through a hard time, our instinct is to directly offer empathy, comfort, solutions, and encouragement. We say things like, "It's okay, you tried your best," or "You'll do better next time." However, all of this goes away the moment we make that mistake. Our internal voice is often critical, harsh, and unforgiving—quite the opposite of how we would ever treat someone. Meghan Markle's quote highlights this double standard by pointing out that true well-being comes from turning that same patience, grace, and forgiveness inward.Beyond this, children should be taught the ideology of treating yourself the same way you would treat someone you love and care for from a young age. A person's inner dialogue forms early on in life and dictates how they handle challenges, pressure, and self-worth. Developing self-respect and self-compassion early in life shapes how a child navigates challenges, builds confidence, and sees themselves in the long run.Treating yourself with the same kindness that you treat others with often reframes mistakes as a normal part of life and growing up.About Meghan Markle’s lifeRachel Meghan Markle was born on August 4, 1981, in Los Angeles, California. Her father worked as a television lighting director and director of photography, whereas her mother worked several jobs, including social work and yoga instruction, to name a few. Markle was interested in the world of Hollywood from a young age. After graduation, she studied theater and international studies, graduating from Northwestern University in 2003.Her career in Hollywood started soon after she graduated, and considered other career options, including a career in diplomacy. She later shifted to acting full-time and scored minor roles in projects like 'Century City,' ‘The War at Home,' ‘CSI: NY,' '90210,' and 'Fringe.' Some of her other work around this time also included ‘Remember Me,' ‘Get Him to the Greek,' and ‘Horrible Bosses.'Meghan Markle’s breakthrough with ‘Suits’In 2011, Markle scored one of her first major roles in the legal drama series 'Suits.' She appeared in more than 100 episodes and stayed on board with the show for around seven seasons. She became a household name in the industry after this; however, she soon after left the acting industry altogether after marrying Prince Harry.About Meghan Markle and Prince HarryThe duo got together after the Prince saw a video of her online and asked their mutual friend about her. Prince Harry and Meghan Markle then met on a blind date in July 2016 that a mutual friend arranged. The two spent a lot of time together following this and started texting each other frequently. Prince Harry soon after invited Markle on a trip to Botswana, which was their first trip together, and the rest is history.The couple got married in the UK in 2018 and served their royal duties as the Duke and Duchess of Sussex until 2020. At the time, they left their royal duties behind and moved to California to raise their family, their children Archie and Lilibet. They stayed in their home in Montecito until recently, when they decided to move back to the UK for an indefinite amount of time.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Mr T taught me a lesson every kid on Chicago's South Side needs to hear
articles.summary: From Robert Taylor Homes to Lake Forest, Mr. T's life proves that faith, hard work and self-respect can overcome even the toughest circumstances.
articles.body: I recently watched the new Netflix documentary on Mr. T. I admit it was disappointing. It felt thin and rushed to me. The filmmakers clearly had no passion for the film since it failed to capture his nature, his complexities, his faith, his service, the hardships and the depth of the road that he traveled. A 48-minute documentary is not enough to do justice to such a life. After all, this is a man who traveled from the rough and violent housing projects known as the Robert Taylor Homes to the top of the world. Still, the documentary reminded me of why Mr. T has always been such an inspirational figure in my life, from my childhood even to now. I hold him up as a role model to my young kids at Project H.O.O.D. His life is one of hard work, doing the right thing and having a dream. Those are not clichés or empty slogans. They are the values that create opportunities in life. Laurence Tureaud was born May 21, 1952, the second-youngest of 12 children on Chicago’s South Side. His father, a minister, left when Laurence was five. His mother, Willie, earned a living cleaning houses in the Lake Forest area of Chicago, and her income to support all her children was supplemented by an $87 monthly welfare check. They were poor, but not in family or spirit. Mr. T talks of how they went to church, loved their mother and stayed away from the gangs. MR. T ON FAITH: 'I ANSWER ONLY TO GOD' One of my favorite Mr. T quotes is, "I was born and raised in the ghetto, but the ghetto was not born and raised in me." Like anyone in the Robert Taylor Homes, he saw violence and all the things that no child should ever see. He also saw racism. He saw white men call his father a "boy." Mr. T was a dreamer who had family around him and who never walked down the wrong path or went to jail because he could not bear to break his mother’s heart. That’s how love can save a child. In the documentary, he talks of how his brother went to fight in Vietnam as a Marine and came home only to be called a "boy." When Laurence was 18, he vowed that no one would ever call him a boy. He changed his name to Mr. T so that the first word out of anyone talking to him would be "Mister." What he was demanding was the respect and dignity that his family had been denied. He respected himself. WHO IS RAISING AMERICA'S CHILDREN? MENTOR WARNS KIDS ARE SEEKING ROLE MODELS ONLINE AS COMMUNITIES FADE At Dunbar Vocational High School, he became a football star and a city wrestling champion. He did not have a fancy gym to build his muscles. He worked out with his brothers on the concrete around the projects. They did push-ups. They did chin-ups from tree branches. They wrestled one another. They built those muscles the honest way. Mr. T won a scholarship to Prairie View A&M, but that did not work out. He moved to the Loop of Chicago because that is where the money was. For me, that is key because he put himself where the opportunity was. He wound up working three jobs at once, and one of them was as a bouncer at a club. It was there that he got the news that his mother had been robbed of her welfare money by thugs in the elevator of the projects. They told her to give them her money or they would cut her throat. Mr. T grabbed his shotgun and went into the projects, where he confronted gang members until he found the people who had made his mother fear for her life. After confronting those responsible, he decided to become a bodyguard. He would protect others the way he believed he had failed to protect his mother. THE WELFARE STATE BROKE BLACK FAMILIES. WORK CAN HELP RESTORE THE DREAM What I love about this story is that he turned what he believed to be a personal failure into a calling. I don’t think it was a personal failure at all, but what he was trying to do in his own way was make the world a better place. He would use his talents and smarts in that way. He didn’t fall into the gang life or anything like that. He created a new pathway in life instead. I don’t know where I read it, but I remember the story of when he was nine years old or so. He told his mother, "One of these days I’m going to be big and strong. I’m going to be a football player and a boxer. I’m going to buy you a beautiful house and pretty dresses." She didn’t laugh at him or mock him. She didn’t doubt him. She instead spoke to him of values and told him that the way to get there was to work hard, save his money and get after it. That’s what Mr. T did. It was those values, not the Hollywood fame, not the gold chains, not the "I pity the fool" line — it was those values that were the engine of his life. NEW STUDY REVEALS THE SINGLE MOST CRITICAL FACTOR IN WHETHER CHILDREN KEEP THEIR FAITH INTO ADULTHOOD That’s the part that I want my kids to hear. Not the mohawk or the tough scowl. I tell them that Mr. T was once just a child like them, born into a bad ZIP code. But he was a dreamer who had family around him and who never walked down the wrong path or went to jail because he could not bear to break his mother’s heart. That’s how love can save a child. And I tell them how Mr. T started at the bottom. He didn’t look for shortcuts or get-rich-quick schemes. He believed in himself, and he created his own opportunities. He used sports to discipline himself, he served his country, and he worked as a janitor, gym teacher and a doorman before anyone called him a "star." He stayed true to himself and made himself so unique that people just wanted to be around him. He was one of a kind and, most of all, he was real, and that’s why the world gravitated toward him. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION We spend far too much time telling the young kids on the South Side that the system or the Man is out to get them. We talk about systemic racism without going anywhere. There’s no hope in any of that. That’s why those conversations just peter out and die when we run out of doom and gloom. And what good does it do to poison a young child’s mind with all that negativity? That’s why I’d rather talk about South Side heroes like Mr. T. His life gives us the simple but brutally honest lesson: Your circumstances are real, and they may be unfair and stacked against you, but they are not your destiny. You are. Your faith, your work, your respect and the dream that you have for yourself — that is your destiny. You have to do the hardest thing in the world, which is to believe in yourself. If you do, you will reach heights you never knew were possible. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP That is the simple truth I tell my kids every day. I even tell that to myself. I know I speak of opportunity all the time, but it is not a political talking point for me. It is the lifesaver. It is the boy who decides that he will buy his mother a house. It is the young man who decides that his circumstances will not define him. It is the man who decides his fate. I pity the fool who looks at Mr. T’s life and still tells our kids they cannot rise. articles.title: How Coventry Market became a CBeebies TV set
articles.summary: The show, filmed in Coventry, aims to help young children explore food through their senses
articles.body:
Coventry Market's fruit and vegetable stalls, fish counters and busy walkways have become an unlikely TV set.

Cameras are rolling among shoppers and traders as local children explore unfamiliar foods for a new CBeebies series.

I Can Taste It aims to help three to six-year-olds build confidence in trying different foods through sight, smell, touch, sound and taste.

Presented by Aaron Roach Bridgeman and puppet co-host Zesty, the programme is being filmed at the market, which producers say offers children an authentic environment in which to learn about food.

"It's important that children see themselves represented in real places with real people," said Dom Sant, founder of Common Story, the Leamington Spa-based company behind the series.

He said the market's atmosphere, variety of stalls and sense of community made it the perfect location.

Among the young participants is six-year-old Oscar, from Bedworth.

His mother, Hannah, said she applied after spotting an advert on social media.

"Oscar loves his food and he's very chatty, so when they met him he made a good impression," she said.

For Hannah, visiting the market has also brought back childhood memories.

"My mum and dad used to bring me here every Saturday morning to do the shopping and I'd always beg to go on the roundabout," she said.

"Every time I walk into the market it's nostalgic. I feel like I'm four years old again, holding my dad's hand."

Director Jess Matthews described filming as a "glorious chaos", with the production team often responding to children's reactions rather than following a strict script.

Alongside Aaron and Zesty, youngsters are also joined by Compost Monster, a character designed to encourage sustainable food habits and reduce food waste.

Market trader David Betts said the production had shone a light on one of Coventry's best-known landmarks.

"It's one of the iconic places in Coventry and people take it for granted," he said.

Fishmonger Clive Miller, whose stall is due to feature in filming, said the programme would help children discover foods they might not normally encounter.

"When children go to the supermarket, they don't get to see fish like this," he said.

"It's a chance for them to learn about a wider variety of fish and where food comes from."

The series is due to air in spring 2027.

Common Story began in a garden shed six years ago with a £10,000 budget. It has since made more than 100 programmes for CBeebies, with a further 30 currently in production.

articles.title: Ed Sheeran responds to Macklemore over Robert Kraft tour boycott claims and Palestine remarks
articles.summary: Macklemore may not be touring with Ed Sheeran any longer but he’s received a wave of public support after New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft insisted he be dropped as a performer.
articles.body: Ed Sheeran was among many who expressed support for Macklemore after the rapper released a statement saying New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft organized a stadium boycott that forced the rapper off Sheeran’s tour. Macklemore, whose real name is Ben Haggerty, alleged Monday that Kraft called Sheeran and threatened to cancel Sheeran’s planned tour stop if Macklemore was still performing. He also alleged that Sheeran told him Kraft rallied other stadium owners to give Sheeran the same ultimatum. The ultimatum came amid criticism of Macklemore for his pro-Palestine remarks during his opening performances for Sheeran’s tour at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. “I told him that if those words were more offensive than the tens of thousands of Palestinian children being killed by Israel, then there was a fundamental disconnect between where those people stood and where I stood,” Macklemore said of his conversation with Sheeran. Sheeran issued a statement Tuesday morning on Instagram, saying it was important to “set out some facts.” He confirmed that he approved Macklemore’s setlist and that venues contacted him, saying they would pull his tour dates after the rapper joined him at MetLife. “I was informed that this stance was based on how Macklemore conveyed part of his message during his performance, rather than everything that was said,” Sheeran said. “I spoke with venues at length all week to try and build a bridge. One of those people was Robert Kraft.” Ultimately, the tour promoter decided to pull Macklemore, Sheeran said. The “Perfect” singer said Macklemore’s contract was with the promoter, not Sheeran. “I am not complicit. I have my personal views on this devastating conflict,” Sheeran said. “Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn’t mean I don’t have them, and it doesn’t mean I don’t care.” He added that he doesn’t use his “professional platform” for politics because the audiences who attend his show come from all backgrounds and “do not expect a political forum.” Sheeran expressed respect for Macklemore and said people can take multiple approaches. Messina Touring Group, the promoter for Sheeran’s tour, told Rolling Stone Monday that it was informed that multiple venues “will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup.” The statement said cancellations would “impact hundreds of thousands of fans,” confirming that Macklemore would no longer perform on his previously scheduled dates. Macklemore’s Instagram post announcing he was dropped from the tour received nearly 800,000 reposts in less than a day. He’s received support from all types of public figures, including fellow artists, actors, activists and internet personalities. Ms. Rachel, the wildly popular children’s content creator whose real name is Rachel Griffin Accurso, posted a statement to her own Instagram account. She criticized Sheeran for trying to show “that we won’t be bullied” into punishing people who support Palestinians. “Instead he caved to people who refuse to accept what the world knows,” Accurso wrote. “A genocide is happening in Gaza. We all need to speak out against it.” A United Nations commission said that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza in findings from an independent inquiry published last year. Israeli government officials have denied the allegations, calling them “distorted and false.” Model Bella Hadid shared Macklemore’s statement to her Instagram Stories on Monday and her sister, Alana, commented on the rapper’s post. Their father, Mohamed Hadid, has previously shared the story of how his family was expelled from their home in Nazareth in the 1948 Nakba, which saw an estimated 750,000 Palestinians forcibly removed in preparation for the founding of Israel. The 29-year-old model did not comment directly on Macklemore’s situation but shared a post by Middle East historian Assal Rad. “Palestinians are so dehumanized that their advocates are punished while their killers roam free,” Rad wrote. “What does it mean for a society that condones rather than condemns the mass slaughter of children?” Kneecap, the Irish artists who successfully fought a terrorism charge in the U.K. over one of its singers waving a flag of the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah, posted a photo with Macklemore to their account. Macklemore is notably of Irish Catholic heritage, as is Ed Sheeran. “All love and solidarity to @macklemore,” Kneecap captioned the post. “FREE PALESTINE.” Dearborn Mayor Abdullah Hammoud invited Macklemore to perform at a concert sponsored by the city and free to the crowd. The Michigan city is home to the largest Arab American community in the country. “Hey @macklemore, if they don’t want you performing in their stadiums, you’re always welcome in Dearborn. Come put on a show here,” Hammoud wrote in a post on X. Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., called it “incredibly disappointing” to see her constituent — Macklemore is a native of Seattle — removed from the tour because of his support for Palestinians. She added that it was a moment to find “moral conscience” and “end this genocide.” “We should all be outraged that powerful people are more upset about what an artist says than the displacement, starvation, and killing of innocent Palestinian children and families,” Jayapal said. “Thank you, Macklemore, for speaking up.” Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., thanked Macklemore in a post on X for “continuing to speak out against the genocide.” “None of us are free until all of us are free,” she wrote. Sports journalist Jemele Hill remarked on the situation in a repost of an announcement that Ye, the rapper formerly known as Kanye West, would be performing at AT&T Stadium in Texas in November. “Man who released a song called Heil Hitler and called himself a Nazi completely welcome to perform in a stadium,” Hill wrote. “Man who said Free Palestine is not.” Sheeran’s tour is scheduled for a stop at the stadium in October. It’s unclear which stadium owners allegedly told Kraft they would join the ultimatum issued to Sheeran. Representatives for AT&T Stadium, which is owned by the city of Arlington, did not immediately respond to a request for comment from NBC News. Macklemore’s own comment section is also filled with support. Celebrities Hannah Einbinder, Marcia Cross and Zara Larson left multiple heart emojis. Podcaster and internet personality Matt Rogers wrote “much respect” in an Instagram comment. Singer Kehlani, who has also been outspoken in her support of Palestinians, wrote that she was behind Macklemore and adored him. “A LOT of the venues / owners are rallied together this way. honored to know you brother,” she wrote. Activist Greta Thunberg wrote, “Full solidarity and free Palestine.” “Artists’ very active silence in the face of injustice and genocide will not be forgotten,” Thunberg commented on Macklemore’s post. In his own statement on Monday, Kraft did not deny Macklemore’s accusations. He said the decision was based on Macklemore’s “recent actions” on stage and “a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community.” Kraft added that the decision was not about trying to stifle Palestinian advocacy or diminishing the suffering of Palestinians. “I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts, because ultimately our goal is the same — peace for all people, an end to suffering, and an end to all hate,” Kraft said.
